sections.h2: Where is the Stark County Recorder, and what can I find there?
sections.html:
The Stark County Recorder is on the first floor of the County Office Building at 110 Central Plaza South, Suite 170, Canton, OH 44702. Its posted window is 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, with no weekend hours. It keeps the permanent record of deeds, mortgages and easements for all land in the county, and the office says those records are searchable on its website around the clock at no direct cost to users.

Stark County is the eighth most populous county in Ohio, with 374,853 residents counted in 2020. Canton is the county seat, and the other cities are Alliance, Canal Fulton, Louisville, Massillon and North Canton. The county covers 581 square miles in northeastern Ohio and was created in 1808.

Not every record sits here. The Recorder's page sends birth and death requests to the Stark County Health Department at 330-493-9904, marriage licenses to the Probate Court at 330-451-7755 and divorce records to the Family Court at 330-451-7415.

sections.h2: What does the Stark County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
The Recorder's fee page opens by saying the office does not set its prices: the Ohio Revised Code does, in section 317.32. The printed schedule lists $34 for a deed's first two pages and $8 for each more, with $4 for each cross reference. The statute also lets counties tack on a small preservation charge, and a county in western Ohio now lists $39 for the same service, so call the Canton office to confirm the figure before you mail a check.

Stark County Recorder price list as published
Document or servicePrinted charge
Deed or mortgage, first two pages$34.00
Every added page$8.00
Cross reference to an earlier document$4.00
Document that fails standardization rules$20.00
Health care power of attorney or living will$34.00
Staff-made copy, per page$2.00

Payment can be cash, check, money order or a card, and cards carry a 2.75 percent convenience fee. Checks go to the Stark County Recorder, and altered checks are refused. A page-count chart on the fee page tabulates totals up to 90 pages.

sections.h2: What must the Stark County Auditor stamp before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate transfer department must endorse the deed first. The Auditor's page says a deed cannot be recorded until it carries the Auditor's stamp showing the conveyance form was filed correctly under Revised Code 319.202. The transfer line is 330-451-7333, with a second number at 330-451-7322.

  • Form DTE 100 states the value on a taxable sale, and DTE 100 (EX) states why a transfer is exempt.
  • Property already receiving the homestead or owner-occupied reduction adds its own statement of conveyance.
  • Stark's printed charge is $.004 of the price rounded up to the next hundred dollars, plus fifty cents per tax parcel.
  • Payment at that counter is by check or cash only.

The Auditor recommends that an attorney prepare the deed, though it allows owners to draft their own. Both options still need the items below.

sections.h2: What belongs on a Stark County deed?
sections.html:
The Auditor's transfer page lists what a deed has to carry:

  • The grantor's marital status, which supports the release of dower rights.
  • The grantee's name and the tax parcel numbers.
  • A current legal description that follows the county's conveyance standards.
  • A reference to the prior deed instrument.
  • The signature of the grantor and of the grantor's spouse if married, whether or not the spouse is on the title.
  • A completed notary clause with the notary's signature.

Deed types the Auditor names include administrator's, commissioner's, executor's, fiduciary, limited and special warranty, quit claim, sheriff's, survivorship, trustee and general warranty deeds. A sheriff's deed needs a description approval form, and a probate transfer arrives as a certificate of transfer or a judgment entry. A transfer on death designation affidavit, unlike most affidavits, does not require a certified death certificate.

sections.h2: When does Stark County require a visit to the tax map office?
sections.html:
The Auditor's page names combinations and splits as the cases that require a visit to the tax map office before the transfer. The same page offers a New Legal Description Application, a Tax Combine and Un-Combine Request and a Condominium Requirements checklist, and a sheriff's deed needs its own description approval form.

A seller of part of a lot or a corner of a farm should therefore call the Auditor's maps line at 330-451-7341 before a closing is scheduled, because a deed cannot be recorded until the Auditor has stamped it. The page also says the office no longer asks for a stamped copy of the previous deed, but the new document must cite it.

sections.h2: Which liens and special filings does the Stark County Recorder accept?
sections.html:
Besides deeds and mortgages, the fee page prices a list of filings that can touch a house sale. Title searchers look for these, and a seller with an unpaid lien should expect a payoff request at closing.

  • Federal tax liens and Department of Justice liens, each with a separate release filing.
  • Abstracts of judgment, which the fee page prices at five dollars.
  • State employment and workers' compensation liens, where the filing itself carries no fee.
  • UCC filings, priced per document and per name indexed.
  • Plats, priced by the square inch on the printed sizes of 11 by 17 up to 24 by 36.

Cross references at $4.00 each link a new document to an earlier recorded one.

sections.h2: Can I record or look up Stark County deeds online?
sections.html:
The Recorder says documents may be recorded electronically, with an E-Recording link on its website, and that the site lets anyone search the records free. Ohio law pushed this along: ORC 317.13 required every recorder to offer e-recording of conveyances and to put indexes and images online for instruments recorded since 1980 by June 30, 2026.

Copies cost nothing online. In the office, a self-serve copy is ten cents a page, and a staff-assisted copy is $2.00 a page. To get a certified copy by mail, send the Recorder a written request, the fee and a stamped self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: Which Stark County school districts and towns appear in deed searches?
sections.html:
Seventeen public school districts serve Stark County, according to Wikipedia: Alliance, Canton City, Canton Local, Fairless, Jackson, Lake, Louisville, Marlington, Massillon, Minerva, North Canton, Northwest, Osnaburg, Perry, Plain, Sandy Valley and Tuslaw. The district name often appears on tax bills and sales listings, so buyers who search deeds by address see it early.

The 2020 census found 85.2 percent of residents living in urban areas and a median age of 42.2, and the county forms the Canton-Massillon metropolitan area within the larger Cleveland-Akron-Canton region. Stark County also borders eight counties: Portage, Mahoning, Columbiana, Carroll, Tuscarawas, Holmes, Wayne and Summit.

faqs.q: What is the Stark County Recorder's address?
faqs.a: Suite 170 at 110 Central Plaza South, Canton, OH 44702, on the first floor of the County Office Building. Posted hours run 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is the Stark County recording fee really $34?
faqs.a: That is the amount on the county's published fee page for a deed's first two pages, with $8 for each added page. State law allows a surcharge of up to $5 per document, so ask the office to confirm the total before mailing.

faqs.q: Do I need the Auditor's stamp before recording in Stark County?
faqs.a: Yes. According to the Auditor's transfer page, recording waits for the Auditor's stamp, which shows the conveyance form was completed correctly. The Auditor accepts only a check or cash for the conveyance fee.

faqs.q: Can the Stark County Recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: Yes, with a 2.75 percent convenience fee added. Cash, checks and money orders are also accepted, and checks should name the Stark County Recorder.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a recorded deed in Stark County?
faqs.a: Ask in person or mail a written request, the fee and a stamped self-addressed envelope. The published price is $2.00 a page for staff-made copies plus $1.00 to certify each document.
